title: Google Cloud Dataflow Production Design Review

questions.question: What is the practical boundary between Apache Beam and Google Cloud Dataflow?
options: Beam defines the pipeline semantics; Dataflow runs that graph on managed distributed infrastructure
Beam provisions Google Cloud workers; Dataflow only stores Python source files
Dataflow defines event-time semantics without pipeline code
They are two names for the same BigQuery connector
questions.explanation: Beam supplies the portable transforms, windows, triggers, and I/O graph. The Dataflow runner plans and executes that graph on managed resources.

questions.question: A stage receives 18,000 records/s. A representative test measured 1,500 records/s per useful worker. How many useful workers does the simple envelope require to stop backlog growth?
questions.explanation: 18,000 divided by 1,500 equals 12. That is a planning requirement, not a prediction that the autoscaler will add workers immediately.

questions.question: The job permits 20 workers, but a keyed stage exposes only 6 useful parallel slots. Why might backlog remain after scaling?
options: Dataflow never supports more than 6 workers
The stage cannot distribute useful work across all configured workers
Exactly-once mode disables keyed transforms
Backlog is measured only for batch jobs
questions.explanation: A worker ceiling is not the same as available parallel work. Hot keys or too few keys can bind throughput before the configured maximum worker count.

questions.question: What does a Beam watermark represent?
options: A promise that no earlier event can ever arrive
The runner's estimate of event-time completeness up to a point
The current worker CPU percentage
The maximum Pub/Sub message size
questions.explanation: A watermark estimates progress in event time. Events for an earlier window can still arrive afterward and are then considered late.

questions.question: What is the main trade-off when allowed lateness is increased?
options: More late events can correct results, but window state and update work remain longer
Workers stop retrying all failed transforms
Every result becomes a processing-time window
The source no longer needs timestamps
questions.explanation: A longer lateness horizon can improve completeness, but it retains state and permits more downstream corrections for longer.

questions.question: Why can an external API call inside a DoFn happen more than once under exactly-once streaming?
options: Exactly-once applies only to batch pipelines
Dataflow may retry transform execution while deduplicating committed pipeline outputs
Triggers always call every external API twice
BigQuery converts every row into two requests
questions.explanation: The service can execute transform code again after failures. Exactly-once committed outputs do not automatically make arbitrary external side effects exactly once.

questions.question: What is the safest treatment for malformed source records?
options: Log the exception and discard the record
Retry the record forever in the main path
Branch it to an observable dead-letter path with repair context and replay identity
Replace every missing field with an empty string
questions.explanation: A dead-letter branch preserves evidence and lets healthy work continue. Stable identity and an idempotent destination make later replay controlled.
